evidence: NUMERICAL ADEQUACY UNRESOLVED: the inherited fractional-weight collision algorithm mixes real weights with integer splitting and an absolute fragment threshold. Its heavy-case replay exhibits large all-or-none collision batches already at decimetre growth and a physically impossible extreme tail. These are exploratory numerical populations, not quantitative snowfall predictions. Removing extreme bins does not validate the smaller population. The audit does not quantify the bias in every case or rule out physical decimetre aggregates. Four conditional one-dimensional, persistent, liquid-saturated cloud calculations. Only cloud-top temperature and depth change relative to the central population cases. Total imposed water supply is fixed at each compared rate; condensation per unit depth therefore increases in a shorter cloud. Single seed, inherited collision/fragmentation laws, no resolved turbulence or large-aggregate mechanical fracture.
reading_rule: Read the attached numerical_assessment and its hash-identified audit before using sizes or deriving storm optics. The assessment changes evidence metadata only; all original numerical results remain intact. Runs have the snow-population/1 run structure, with cloud_depth_m added. Compare top -5 and -10 C to the same-rate top -15 C population case; do not infer cloud occurrence from these imposed depths. Summaries weight arriving mass; number and area bins retain their original moments. The 100/L parameter normalizes injected number flux with the speed of a 0.2 mm crystal, not a fixed size-resolved concentration boundary. Dendrite-area geometry is held for the controlled comparison; warmer cloud tops do not establish dendritic crystal production. These runs retain a saturated column rather than the intermittent dry gaps in archived weather.
